intro.title: Error handling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js application that handles errors gracefully when reading a file. You will learn the core concept of error handling using try-catch blocks to manage and respond to runtime errors. The main technologies involved are Node.js's built-in 'fs' module for file operations and JavaScript's error handling constructs. By the end, you'll understand how to prevent crashes and provide useful feedback when things go wrong in your code.
intro.usecase: Error handling is essential in any Node.js application that interacts with external systems or user input. In real products, this appears when APIs fail to respond, database connections drop, or users submit invalid data in forms. For example, an e-commerce checkout system must gracefully handle payment gateway errors by showing user-friendly messages instead of crashing. A dashboard displaying analytics needs to manage failed data fetches by showing fallback content or retry options. Proper error handling ensures applications remain stable and provide helpful feedback rather than cryptic technical failures.
